newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge rises as rumours take root.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge rises as rumours take root.

text.p: Belgian insurer Royale Belge SA rose another three percent in early trade on Monday as rumours that a merger operation with AXA Belgium was in the offing took root.

Royale Belge was up 2.89 percent at 9,250 francs at 0940 GMT after earlier hitting 9,350 francs, a new all-time high. The share also rose 4.20 percent on Friday in the wake of news on Thursday that exceptional gains pushed 1996 profit to 11.3 billion Belgian francs and that the company would pay a bonus dividend. The company also said on Thursday its share was worth nearer 10,000 Belgian francs.

"It's pure speculation," said KB Securities analyst Dirk Peters. "The only surprise in the results was the bonus dividend but that does not justify a 10 percent rise in the share price. There's more going on."

"I think it's a combination of...the bonus dividend that was not expected and speculation about what is going on between AXA/UAP and a possible merger between AXA Belgium and Royale Belge," Generale Bank analyst Martine Deroanne said.
The planned merger of French insurance group's AXA and UAP to form AXA-UAP has left analysts pondering the fate of the new French group's Belgian units.
AXA Belgium chief executive officer Patrick de Courcel said on March 5 that a closer link with Royale Belge, a unit of UAP, was "the natural scenario".
However, presenting 1996 results last Thursday Royale Belge chief executive officer Jean-Pierre Gerard declined to comment.
Working groups had been set up to examine the issue and the results should be known and announced by May, he said.

Analysts said it was too early to speculate on how a merger between Royale Belge and AXA Belgium might work in practice. Some have speculated that AXA-UAP might first raise its interest in Royale Belge before any move.
Royale Belge is owned 51.20 percent owned by Royale Vendome SA an investment vehicle 25.10 percent held by Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA and 74.90 percent by AXA-UAP units.

"There are some speculative stories in the market and every one involves Royale Belge," KB Securities analyst Peters said, noting separate rumours surrounding the future of bank Banque Bruxelles Lambert SA, in which Royale Belge and GBL each own around 12.5 percent.
